words.enDefinition: economic analysis of how firms organise production and make decisions about inputs, output and pricing

examples.en: The theory of the firm helped the class explain why the workshop hired labour before expanding its premises.
examples.zh: 「厂商理论」帮助同学们解释为什么车间先增聘人手，再扩大经营场地。

examples.en: We applied the theory of the firm to compare the producer's decisions under different competitive conditions.
examples.zh: 我们运用「厂商理论」，比较该生产者在不同竞争条件下的决策。

collocations: study the theory of the firm
apply the theory of the firm
an assumption in the theory of the firm

words.enDefinition: the methods and feasible relationships determining what output can be produced from available inputs

examples.en: The model assumed the same production technology for both workshops before comparing their choices of labour and machines.
examples.zh: 模型先假定两家车间采用同一种「生产技术」，再比较它们对劳动和机器的选择。

examples.en: We discussed how changes in production technology might increase output without increasing resource use.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「生产技术」的变化如何在资源用量不增加的情况下提高产量。

words.enDefinition: an input whose quantity cannot be changed during the period being analysed

examples.en: In the short-run example, the oven was a fixed input because adding another would take several months.
examples.zh: 在短期示例中，增设烤炉需要几个月，因此现有烤炉属于「固定投入要素」。

examples.en: The tutor asked which fixed input limited the number of bicycles the workshop could repair each day.
examples.zh: 导师问，哪项「固定投入要素」限制了车间每天能修的自行车数量。

words.enDefinition: an input whose quantity can be adjusted within the time period being analysed

examples.en: Labour hours were a variable input because the stall could adjust them each day in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的摊位每天都能调整人工工时，所以工时是「可变投入要素」。

examples.en: We added one unit of the variable input while keeping the size of the kitchen unchanged.
examples.zh: 我们增加一个单位的「可变投入要素」，厨房面积维持原样。

collocations: choose the amount of a variable input

words.enDefinition: a relationship between variable inputs and feasible output when at least one other input is fixed

examples.en: The short-run production function showed how extra workers affected output while the number of machines stayed fixed.
examples.zh: 「短期生产函数」显示机器台数固定时，增加工人怎样影响产量。

examples.en: We drew the short-run production function after selecting a particular workshop size for the first part.
examples.zh: 为第一部分选定一个车间规模后，我们画出了「短期生产函数」。

words.enDefinition: the quantity of output produced with the amounts of inputs specified in the production analysis

examples.en: The total product rose when the bakery added a worker while continuing to use the same equipment.
examples.zh: 面包店增加一名工人、继续使用同一套设备时，「总产量」上升了。

examples.en: We recorded total product for each staffing level before calculating how much output an extra worker added.
examples.zh: 我们记录各用工水平下的「总产量」，再计算增聘一名工人带来的额外产出。

collocations: plot total product against labour input

words.enDefinition: output per unit of a specified input, calculated by dividing total output by the quantity of that input

examples.en: The average product of labour fell when additional staff had to share the same small work surface.
examples.zh: 额外雇用的员工也要共用同一个狭小工作台时，劳动的「平均产量」下降了。

examples.en: We calculated average product for each group using the total number of units and hours worked.
examples.zh: 我们用各组的总件数和工时计算「平均产量」。

collocations: compare average product with marginal product

words.enDefinition: additional output from increasing one input by a unit, or the rate of change for a continuous input

examples.en: The marginal product of another worker was low because all the packing tables were already in use.
examples.zh: 打包台已全部占用，再增加一名工人的「边际产量」很低。

examples.en: We compared the marginal product at different staffing levels while keeping oven capacity fixed in the example.
examples.zh: 示例里我们固定烤炉容量，比较不同用工水平下的「边际产量」。

collocations: measure the marginal product of an input
compare marginal product across input levels

words.enDefinition: the change in output per additional unit of labour when other input amounts are held constant

examples.en: The marginal product of labour declined after the fourth worker joined the already crowded preparation area.
examples.zh: 第四名工人加入本来就拥挤的准备区后，「劳动的边际产量」下降了。

examples.en: We calculated the marginal product of labour using output changes at a fixed number of packing tables.
examples.zh: 打包台台数固定时，我们根据产量变化计算「劳动的边际产量」。

collocations: calculate the marginal product of labour
compare the marginal product of labour with the wage
plot the marginal product of labour

words.enDefinition: the change in output per additional unit of physical capital when other inputs are held constant

examples.en: The marginal product of capital measured the extra output from adding a machine without changing staffing.
examples.zh: 「资本的边际产量」衡量保持人员不变、增加一台机器带来的额外产出。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether the marginal product of capital changed when the plant had three machines.
examples.zh: 导师问，工厂拥有三台机器时，「资本的边际产量」是否发生变化。

collocations: estimate the marginal product of capital
compare the marginal product of capital across plants
plot the marginal product of capital

words.enDefinition: a graph of total output against the amount of a varied input, holding other inputs fixed

examples.en: The total product curve flattened as more workers shared the same equipment in the production example.
examples.zh: 生产示例中，随着更多工人共用同一设备，「总产量曲线」逐渐变平。

examples.en: We read two points on the total product curve to calculate the output change between them.
examples.zh: 我们读取「总产量曲线」上的两点，计算两点之间的产量变化。

collocations: read the slope of a total product curve

words.enDefinition: a graph showing how the marginal product of an input changes with the amount of that input

examples.en: The marginal product curve bent down after additional staff began sharing the same preparation area.
examples.zh: 新增员工开始共用同一准备区后，「边际产量曲线」向下弯折。

examples.en: We plotted the marginal product curve using the increases in output shown in the production table.
examples.zh: 我们用生产表中列出的产量增量绘制「边际产量曲线」。

collocations: find the peak of a marginal product curve

words.enDefinition: the tendency for successive units of a variable input eventually to add less output when other inputs stay fixed

examples.en: The law of diminishing marginal returns explained why extra workers contributed less once the bench became crowded.
examples.zh: 「边际报酬递减规律」解释了为什么工作台拥挤后，再增聘工人所带来的产量更少。

examples.en: We illustrated the law of diminishing marginal returns by adding workers while holding the number of ovens constant.
examples.zh: 我们维持烤炉台数不变、逐步增聘工人，以说明「边际报酬递减规律」。

collocations: illustrate the law of diminishing marginal returns
apply the law of diminishing marginal returns
an example of the law of diminishing marginal returns

words.enDefinition: a drop in total output when the amount of a particular input is increased with other inputs fixed

examples.en: The negative marginal product meant that adding another worker actually reduced output in the overcrowded stall.
examples.zh: 「负的边际产量」表示，在这个过于拥挤的摊位上增加一名工人反而降低产量。

examples.en: We identified negative marginal product where the total output curve sloped downward as staffing rose further.
examples.zh: 人数继续增加而总产量曲线下降时，我们识别出「负的边际产量」。

words.enDefinition: the units of labour used for each unit of capital in a production method

examples.en: The labour-capital ratio rose when the producer kept its equipment and paid for more staffing hours.
examples.zh: 生产者保留原有设备，同时增加有薪工时，「劳动资本比」随之上升。

examples.en: We compared the labour-capital ratio of two techniques that produced the same number of finished bags.
examples.zh: 我们比较了能做出相同成品包数量的两种生产方法的「劳动资本比」。

words.enDefinition: the reliance of a production method on labour relative to other inputs such as capital

examples.en: The workshop's labour intensity fell after it installed equipment that could handle some of the manual sorting.
examples.zh: 车间安装能承担一部分人工分拣的设备后，「劳动密集程度」下降了。

examples.en: We compared labour intensity across two methods that used very different amounts of equipment per worker.
examples.zh: 我们比较了人均设备量差别很大的两种方法的「劳动密集程度」。

words.enDefinition: achieving the maximum feasible output from given inputs, or using no more inputs than needed for a given output

examples.en: The exercise described technical efficiency by asking whether the same workers and equipment could produce more output.
examples.zh: 练习询问同样的人手和设备能否生产更多，以说明「技术效率」。

examples.en: We compared technical efficiency before examining which workshop faced cheaper input prices in the example.
examples.zh: 我们先比较「技术效率」，再看示例中哪家车间面对更低的投入要素价格。

collocations: measure a loss of technical efficiency

words.enDefinition: a curve showing combinations of inputs that produce the same specified amount of output

examples.en: The production isoquant showed how more machine hours could substitute for some labour at unchanged output.
examples.zh: 「等产量曲线」显示在产量不变时，增用机器工时如何替代一部分人工。

examples.en: We drew a production isoquant for one hundred units before considering any changes in input prices.
examples.zh: 考虑投入要素价格变化之前，我们先画出产量为一百件的「等产量曲线」。

collocations: choose a point on a production isoquant

words.enDefinition: a set of isoquants showing feasible input combinations for several levels of output

examples.en: The isoquant map placed the curve for higher output farther from the origin in our example.
examples.zh: 在示例中，「等产量曲线图」把较高产量的曲线画在离原点更远的位置。

examples.en: We used an isoquant map to see how the required input combinations changed as output increased.
examples.zh: 我们用「等产量曲线图」查看产量提高时所需的投入组合怎样变化。

collocations: interpret output changes on an isoquant map

words.enDefinition: a line showing the input combinations that have the same total expenditure at specified input prices

examples.en: The isocost line showed combinations of worker hours and rented machine hours that cost the same amount.
examples.zh: 「等成本线」显示了总费用相同的人工工时和租用机器工时的组合。

examples.en: We redrew the isocost line after the machine hire price fell and the wage stayed unchanged.
examples.zh: 机器租用价格下降、工资保持不变时，我们重新画了「等成本线」。

collocations: find a point on an isocost line

words.enDefinition: the negative ratio of the prices of the horizontal-axis input and the vertical-axis input on an isocost graph

examples.en: The isocost slope became more negative when the wage rose and labour was measured on the horizontal axis.
examples.zh: 工资上升且劳动量画在横轴上时，「等成本线斜率」变得更负。

examples.en: We compared the isocost slope in the two diagrams to see how the relative input prices differed.
examples.zh: 我们比较两张图中的「等成本线斜率」，了解投入要素的相对价格如何不同。

collocations: compare the isocost slope with the isoquant slope

words.enDefinition: the rate at which one input can replace another while output is held constant along an isoquant

examples.en: The marginal rate of technical substitution fell as the firm moved toward using more labour along the isoquant.
examples.zh: 厂商沿等产量曲线增加劳动用量时，「边际技术替代率」下降了。

examples.en: We calculated the marginal rate of technical substitution from two marginal products in the smooth example.
examples.zh: 在使用平滑曲线的示例中，我们根据两项边际产量求出「边际技术替代率」。

collocations: calculate the marginal rate of technical substitution
compare the marginal rate of technical substitution with relative input prices
interpret the marginal rate of technical substitution

words.expression: diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution
words.lemma: diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution
words.enDefinition: the pattern in which additional units of one input replace progressively smaller amounts of another at the same output
acceptedEnVariants: diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution

examples.en: A diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution meant each additional worker replaced fewer machine hours along the curve.
examples.zh: 沿曲线增加一名工人所能替代的机器工时越来越少，体现了「边际技术替代率递减」。

examples.en: We drew a curved isoquant to illustrate a diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在练习中画出一条弯曲的等产量曲线，以演示「边际技术替代率递减」。

collocations: illustrate a diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution
assume a diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution
an isoquant with a diminishing marginal rate of technical substitution

words.enDefinition: the extent to which different inputs can replace each other while producing the same output

examples.en: The model compared input substitutability between firms using flexible tools and firms using a fixed assembly process.
examples.zh: 模型对比采用灵活工具的厂商与采用固定装配流程的厂商的「投入要素的可替代性」。

examples.en: We discussed whether input substitutability would allow a producer to adjust after either input became more expensive.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了任一投入要素价格上涨后，「投入要素的可替代性」能否让生产者作出调整。

collocations: compare the degree of input substitutability

words.zhGloss: 完全可替代的投入要素
words.enDefinition: production inputs that can replace one another at a fixed rate without changing output
acceptedZhAnswers: 完全可替代的投入要素

examples.en: The worksheet used perfectly substitutable inputs that provided the same work per hour on either machine.
examples.zh: 练习设定两台机器每小时完成相同工作，把它们视为「完全可替代的投入要素」。

examples.en: We drew a straight isoquant in the example with perfectly substitutable inputs and a fixed replacement rate.
examples.zh: 在「完全可替代的投入要素」按固定比率互换的示例中，我们画了一条直线形的等产量曲线。

collocations: draw an isoquant for perfectly substitutable inputs

words.enDefinition: a technology in which inputs need to be used in specified proportions to increase output

examples.en: The fixed-proportions technology required one bench for each worker before another unit could be produced.
examples.zh: 按这项「固定比例生产技术」，每名工人都要配一个工作台，产量才能增加。

examples.en: Our tutor used fixed-proportions technology to explain why one unused input alone could add no output.
examples.zh: 导师用「固定比例生产技术」说明为什么单独增加某种尚有余量的投入不会增加产量。

collocations: draw an isoquant for fixed-proportions technology

words.enDefinition: a fixed-proportions production function in which output is limited by the smallest effective input quantity

examples.en: The Leontief production function made extra tool sets unproductive unless the number of trained operators also increased.
examples.zh: 在「列昂惕夫生产函数」下，若受训操作员人数没有增加，多出的工具套装不会提高产量。

examples.en: We drew the right-angled isoquant implied by the Leontief production function used in our example.
examples.zh: 我们画出了示例「列昂惕夫生产函数」所对应的直角等产量曲线。

collocations: derive isoquants from a Leontief production function

words.zhGloss: 柯布道格拉斯生产函数
words.enDefinition: a production function multiplying a productivity factor by input quantities each raised to a specified power
acceptedZhAnswers: 柯布道格拉斯生产函数

examples.en: The Cobb-Douglas production function let us vary labour and capital together and compare the resulting output.
examples.zh: 「柯布道格拉斯生产函数」使我们能同时改变劳动和资本用量，再比较产量。

examples.en: We checked the input exponents in the Cobb-Douglas production function before classifying its returns to scale.
examples.zh: 我们检查了「柯布道格拉斯生产函数」中各投入项的指数，再判断其规模报酬类型。

collocations: compute marginal products from a Cobb-Douglas production function

words.enDefinition: a specified combination of quantities of the inputs available to a producer

examples.en: The first input bundle required fewer work hours but more machine hours than the alternative bundle.
examples.zh: 第一种「投入组合」需要较少人工工时，却比另一组合需要更多机器工时。

examples.en: We chose the input bundle that met the required output at the lowest cost in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，我们选择以最低成本达到指定产量的「投入组合」。

words.enDefinition: a set of input amounts that achieves a given output while minimising total input expense

examples.en: The least-cost input combination changed when rented machine hours became cheaper but the wage stayed the same.
examples.zh: 机器租用工时降价而工资不变时，「成本最低的投入组合」变了。

examples.en: We found the least-cost input combination by comparing the feasible points shown on the target isoquant.
examples.zh: 我们比较目标等产量曲线上的可行点，找到了「成本最低的投入组合」。

collocations: calculate the expense of a least-cost input combination

words.zhGloss: 投入选择的内点最优解
words.enDefinition: a best feasible input combination lying away from the boundaries, generally using positive quantities of all relevant inputs
acceptedZhAnswers: 投入选择的内点最优解

examples.en: An interior input optimum used both production inputs in positive quantities under the conditions of the example.
examples.zh: 在示例条件下，「投入选择的内点最优解」中两种生产要素的用量都为正。

examples.en: We compared the interior input optimum with an alternative where the producer used only one input.
examples.zh: 我们将「投入选择的内点最优解」与生产者只用一种要素的方案作了比较。

collocations: check conditions for an interior input optimum
compare an interior input optimum with a corner solution

words.enDefinition: the input quantities a firm chooses to minimise cost for a specified output level and set of input prices

examples.en: The conditional factor demand for labour fell when wages rose while target output and equipment prices stayed fixed.
examples.zh: 目标产量和设备价格不变、工资上涨时，劳动的「有条件要素需求」下降了。

examples.en: Our tutor derived conditional factor demand by fixing output before solving the model's input choice problem.
examples.zh: 导师先固定产量，再解模型中的投入选择问题，得出「有条件要素需求」。

collocations: compare conditional factor demands across output targets

words.enDefinition: the curve joining least-cost input combinations at different output levels while input prices remain fixed

examples.en: The cost expansion path connected the producer's least-cost choices for small, medium and large output levels.
examples.zh: 「成本最小化扩张路径」连接生产者在低、中、高产量下成本最低的选择。

examples.en: We traced the cost expansion path without changing the input prices used to draw the graph.
examples.zh: 我们保持作图所用的要素价格不变，描出了「成本最小化扩张路径」。

collocations: derive a cost expansion path from input choices

words.enDefinition: an opportunity cost of using resources already owned by the firm without directly paying for them

examples.en: The owner gave up rental income by using her building, so the model included an implicit cost.
examples.zh: 业主自己使用楼宇而放弃了租金收入，所以模型计入一项「隐性成本」。

examples.en: We estimated the implicit cost of the organizer's time before comparing the project's alternative uses of labour.
examples.zh: 比较这个项目的其他用工方案前，我们估算了组织者时间的「隐性成本」。

collocations: compare an implicit cost with a cash expense

words.enDefinition: total revenue minus all explicit and implicit economic costs of using the firm's resources

examples.en: The economic profit fell after we included the earnings the owner could have received in another occupation.
examples.zh: 计入业主从事其他职业原本能获得的收入后，「经济利润」下降了。

examples.en: We compared economic profit for two producers that reported the same accounting profit but owned different assets.
examples.zh: 两家生产者报告的会计利润相同，但拥有的资产不同，我们比较了它们的「经济利润」。

collocations: account for opportunity costs when calculating economic profit

words.enDefinition: the minimum return needed to keep the entrepreneur's resources in their current activity, included in economic cost

examples.en: The tutor counted normal profit as part of the opportunity cost of keeping capital in the shop.
examples.zh: 导师把「正常利润」视为让资本留在店里的机会成本的一部分。

examples.en: The small producer earned normal profit because its return matched the owner's best alternative use of those resources.
examples.zh: 小生产者的回报恰好等于业主将资源投入最佳替代用途的回报，因此获得的是「正常利润」。

collocations: include normal profit among economic costs

words.enDefinition: a situation where total revenue exactly covers explicit and implicit economic costs, including normal returns

examples.en: The firm had zero economic profit even though the owner received a return covering her invested resources.
examples.zh: 这家厂商的「经济利润为零」，业主仍获得了足以覆盖自有资源机会成本的回报。

examples.en: Entry stopped at zero economic profit in the simplified long-run model with identical firms and no barriers.
examples.zh: 在厂商相同且无壁垒的简化长期模型中，进入在「经济利润为零」时停止。

collocations: show zero economic profit in equilibrium

words.enDefinition: the sum of fixed and variable costs divided by the quantity of output

examples.en: The average total cost fell as the workshop initially distributed the same rent across more completed orders.
examples.zh: 起初，车间将同一笔租金分摊到更多完工订单上，「平均总成本」下降了。

examples.en: We compared price with average total cost to see whether the model firm made an economic profit.
examples.zh: 我们将价格与「平均总成本」比较，判断模型中的厂商是否获得经济利润。

collocations: compare price with average total cost

words.enDefinition: a graph of average cost at different output levels when at least one input is fixed

examples.en: The short-run average cost curve used one workshop size while the number of completed orders could vary.
examples.zh: 「短期平均成本曲线」假定车间规模固定，而完工订单数量可以变化。

examples.en: We drew another short-run average cost curve for the larger building shown in the practice exercise.
examples.zh: 我们为练习里较大的楼宇另画了一条「短期平均成本曲线」。

collocations: draw a short-run average cost curve
read a short-run average cost curve
compare short-run average cost curves for two plants

words.enDefinition: a graph of the lowest attainable average cost at each output level when all inputs may be adjusted

examples.en: The long-run average cost curve showed the cheapest plant size at each planned output in our model.
examples.zh: 「长期平均成本曲线」显示模型中各计划产量所对应的最低成本厂房规模。

examples.en: The tutor traced the long-run average cost curve beneath the alternatives available at different plant sizes.
examples.zh: 导师沿各种厂房规模所对应曲线的下包络，描出了「长期平均成本曲线」。

collocations: derive a long-run average cost curve
move along the long-run average cost curve
locate the minimum of the long-run average cost curve

words.enDefinition: a graph of the extra cost of producing additional output when at least one input is fixed

examples.en: The short-run marginal cost curve rose after extra orders required increasingly expensive overtime at the same workshop.
examples.zh: 同一车间接到额外订单后必须付出越来越高的加班成本，「短期边际成本曲线」随之上升。

examples.en: We read the short-run marginal cost curve to find the cost of producing the next finished item.
examples.zh: 我们读取「短期边际成本曲线」，找出再生产一件成品的成本。

collocations: draw a short-run marginal cost curve
read a short-run marginal cost curve
derive the short-run marginal cost curve from total cost

words.enDefinition: a graph of the additional cost of expanding output when the firm is free to adjust all inputs

examples.en: The long-run marginal cost curve reflected changes in capacity as output increased in our model.
examples.zh: 在我们的模型里，「长期边际成本曲线」反映了产量增加时产能也能变化。

examples.en: We derived the long-run marginal cost curve from the least total cost at nearby output levels.
examples.zh: 我们根据相邻几个产量水平的最低总成本，推导出「长期边际成本曲线」。

collocations: derive the long-run marginal cost curve
interpret a long-run marginal cost curve
compare long-run and short-run marginal cost curves

words.enDefinition: a graph of total production cost for different output levels in a period when some input is fixed

examples.en: The short-run total cost curve started above zero because the workshop still paid rent without producing anything.
examples.zh: 车间没有产出时仍要付房租，所以「短期总成本曲线」从零以上起步。

examples.en: We compared two points on the short-run total cost curve to calculate the cost of increased production.
examples.zh: 我们比较「短期总成本曲线」上的两点，计算增产所需的成本。

collocations: plot a short-run total cost curve
measure the slope of the short-run total cost curve

words.enDefinition: the lower boundary formed by choosing the least costly among several cost curves at each output level

examples.en: The cost envelope traced the lowest available average cost across three possible factory sizes in our diagram.
examples.zh: 我们图中的「成本包络线」沿三种可选工厂规模中能达到的最低平均成本画出。

examples.en: We read the cost envelope to see when a larger plant became cheaper for a given output.
examples.zh: 我们读取「成本包络线」，判断在给定产量下何时采用更大的工厂成本更低。

collocations: derive a long-run curve as a cost envelope

words.enDefinition: how output changes when all production inputs are multiplied by the same factor

examples.en: The tutor measured returns to scale by doubling labour and equipment together in the production example.
examples.zh: 导师在生产示例中同时将劳动和设备用量加倍，以衡量「规模报酬」。

examples.en: We compared returns to scale for two production functions using the same proportional change in both inputs.
examples.zh: 我们将两种投入同时按相同比例改变，比较两个生产函数的「规模报酬」。

collocations: classify a production function by its returns to scale

words.enDefinition: a case where a common proportional increase in all inputs increases output by the same proportion

examples.en: With constant returns to scale, doubling the available machinery and staff doubled output in the example.
examples.zh: 在示例中，机器和人手同时加倍时，产量也加倍，表现为「规模报酬不变」。

examples.en: The tutor drew rays through the production diagram to illustrate constant returns to scale across different sizes.
examples.zh: 导师在生产图里画出射线，说明规模变化时怎样体现「规模报酬不变」。

collocations: test for constant returns to scale

words.enDefinition: a case where output grows by a greater proportion than the common proportional increase in all inputs

examples.en: The example showed increasing returns to scale when doubling both inputs more than doubled output.
examples.zh: 示例中把两种投入都加倍，成品数却增至两倍以上，表现为「规模报酬递增」。

examples.en: The tutor asked why increasing returns to scale could hold while one input's marginal product was diminishing.
examples.zh: 导师问，一种投入要素的边际产量在递减时，为什么仍可能出现「规模报酬递增」。

collocations: distinguish increasing returns to scale from diminishing marginal returns

words.enDefinition: a case where output grows by a smaller proportion than the common proportional increase in all inputs

examples.en: Our decreasing returns to scale example produced less than twice as much output after doubling the two inputs.
examples.zh: 在「规模报酬递减」的示例里，两种投入加倍后，产量没有达到两倍。

examples.en: We looked for decreasing returns to scale by scaling every input together across several points in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，我们在几个不同点同时等比例增加各项投入，判断是否有「规模报酬递减」。

collocations: test for decreasing returns to scale

words.enDefinition: the increase in long-run average cost as production expands beyond the relevant scale

examples.en: The diseconomies of scale in our example came from coordinating deliveries across too many separate workshops.
examples.zh: 示例中的「规模不经济」来自为过多分开的车间协调配送。

examples.en: We looked for diseconomies of scale on the upward-sloping part of the long-run average cost curve.
examples.zh: 我们在长期平均成本曲线的上升段找「规模不经济」。

collocations: explain a source of diseconomies of scale

words.enDefinition: the smallest output level at which long-run average cost reaches its minimum

examples.en: The minimum efficient scale was the first output level on the flat bottom of the long-run cost curve.
examples.zh: 长期平均成本曲线的底部为平段，进入平段的第一个产量就是「最小有效规模」。

examples.en: We compared the minimum efficient scale with estimated market demand in the example involving many small buyers.
examples.zh: 我们在涉及大量小买家的示例中，把「最小有效规模」与估计的市场需求作了比较。

collocations: compare minimum efficient scale with market size

words.enDefinition: a cost advantage from producing multiple outputs together rather than producing them separately

examples.en: We found economies of scope when one kitchen could prepare both menus more cheaply than two separate kitchens.
examples.zh: 一个厨房制作两套菜单的成本比两个厨房分开做更低，我们发现了「范围经济」。

examples.en: The producer benefited from economies of scope because the same delivery route could handle both kinds of orders.
examples.zh: 同一条配送线路可以送两种订单，生产者因此受益于「范围经济」。

words.enDefinition: higher cost from producing different outputs jointly than from providing each separately

examples.en: The sample bakery encountered diseconomies of scope because switching between products required costly cleaning and repeated setup.
examples.zh: 示例面包店切换产品时要付出较高的清洁费用并反复做准备，出现了「范围不经济」。

examples.en: We compared the joint costs with separate production costs to look for diseconomies of scope in our model.
examples.zh: 我们比较联合生产和分开生产的成本，判断模型中是否出现「范围不经济」。

words.enDefinition: improving productivity through accumulated experience performing production tasks

examples.en: To estimate learning by doing, the group compared production times across batches of identical items.
examples.zh: 为估算「干中学」的效果，小组比较了生产多批相同产品的耗时。

examples.en: The model separated learning by doing from the lower input prices the firm negotiated over time.
examples.zh: 模型将「干中学」与厂商后来谈到的更低投入要素价格区分开。

collocations: measure the gains from learning by doing

words.enDefinition: a producer's decision about the productive capacity to install before future output is known or chosen

examples.en: The capacity choice depended on whether the expected number of orders justified adding a larger oven.
examples.zh: 预计订单量能否抵消增设更大烤炉的成本，影响了「产能选择」。

examples.en: We compared the capacity choice under low and high demand forecasts in the model for the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们在车间模型中比较需求预测偏低和偏高时的「产能选择」。

words.enDefinition: the competitive organisation of a market, including the number and size of firms and the nature of their products

examples.en: The market structure differed between the farm example with many sellers and the example with one utility.
examples.zh: 农场示例有许多卖家，公用事业示例只有一家，两者的「市场结构」不同。

examples.en: We examined market structure before deciding whether the model firm could influence the price it charged.
examples.zh: 判断模型厂商能否影响自己所收的价格前，我们先研究「市场结构」。

words.enDefinition: the extent to which activity in an industry is accounted for by a relatively small number of firms

examples.en: The industry concentration measure rose after two of the larger firms came under the same ownership.
examples.zh: 两家较大的厂商归于同一所有者后，「行业集中度」指标上升了。

examples.en: We checked how the defined market affected the estimate of industry concentration in the class exercise.
examples.zh: 我们检查课堂练习中市场的定义如何影响「行业集中度」的估计。

collocations: report a change in industry concentration

words.enDefinition: the combined market share of the four largest firms in a defined market

examples.en: The four-firm concentration ratio increased because the four biggest suppliers captured a larger share of sales.
examples.zh: 最大四家供应商占据了更大销售份额，「四企业集中率」因此上升。

examples.en: We calculated the four-firm concentration ratio before comparing it with a measure that included all sellers.
examples.zh: 我们计算「四企业集中率」，再与计入所有卖家的指标作比较。

collocations: interpret changes in the four-firm concentration ratio

words.enDefinition: a market concentration measure calculated by summing the squares of firms' market shares

examples.en: The class used the Herfindahl-Hirschman index to compare two markets with equally many firms but differently distributed sales.
examples.zh: 我们班用「赫芬达尔赫希曼指数」比较厂商数量相同、销售份额分布不同的两个市场。

examples.en: We calculated the Herfindahl-Hirschman index after converting each firm's share to the units specified in class.
examples.zh: 我们把各厂商份额转换成课堂规定的单位后，计算了「赫芬达尔赫希曼指数」。

words.enDefinition: a model with many price-taking producers, a homogeneous product, and no substantial barriers to entry or exit

examples.en: Under perfect competition, the small seller in our exercise could sell at the market price without influencing it.
examples.zh: 在「完全竞争」下，练习中的小卖家可以按市场价格销售，但无法影响该价格。

examples.en: We compared perfect competition with a case where producers could set different prices for differentiated products.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「完全竞争」和生产者可以对差异化产品收取不同价格的情形。

collocations: analyse a market under perfect competition

words.enDefinition: a market participant that treats the prevailing market price as given when choosing how much to buy or sell

examples.en: Each producer was a price taker since its sales were small relative to the whole market.
examples.zh: 在农场模型中，各生产者的销量与整个市场相比很小，所以都是「价格接受者」。

examples.en: The tutor asked what would happen if one price taker tried charging above the prevailing market price.
examples.zh: 导师问，如果一个「价格接受者」尝试报出高于现行市场价格的售价，结果会怎样。

collocations: assume a firm is a price taker
describe the behaviour of a price taker

words.enDefinition: in the perfectly competitive model, a producer that chooses how much to sell while taking the market price as given

examples.en: The competitive firm adjusted its output after the market price fell, without setting a separate price itself.
examples.zh: 面对市场价格下跌，「竞争性厂商」调整了产量，自己没有另行定价。

examples.en: We graphed cost curves for the competitive firm before estimating how much it would sell.
examples.zh: 估计「竞争性厂商」会卖多少之前，我们先画了它的成本曲线。

collocations: analyse output for a competitive firm
calculate the profit of a competitive firm

words.enDefinition: a product buyers treat as equivalent regardless of which seller provides it in the market model

examples.en: The model assumed a homogeneous product, so customers regarded flour from the different farms as interchangeable.
examples.zh: 模型假定面粉为「同质产品」，因此顾客认为不同农场的面粉可以互相替代。

examples.en: We tested whether the market for a homogeneous product still allowed differences in delivery times in the case.
examples.zh: 我们检验案例中「同质产品」市场是否仍允许交付时间有差异。

collocations: compete in a market with a homogeneous product

words.enDefinition: a market condition where producers can join or leave without substantial barriers

examples.en: With free entry and exit, profitable market conditions could attract new firms in the long-run example.
examples.zh: 在长期示例里，由于有「自由进入与退出」，可盈利的市场条件会吸引新厂商。

examples.en: The tutor contrasted free entry and exit with a model requiring extended exclusive rights to supply the service.
examples.zh: 导师把「自由进入与退出」与必须持有长期排他供应权的模型作了比较。

collocations: model a market with free entry and exit

words.enDefinition: the condition for an interior output optimum for a price-taking firm with differentiable costs, subject to profitability and second-order conditions

examples.en: The tutor checked where price equals marginal cost before deciding whether the competitive producer should operate.
examples.zh: 导师先检查何处「价格等于边际成本」，再判断这个竞争性生产者是否应该开工。

examples.en: Our diagram marked the point where price equals marginal cost on the increasing part of the cost curve.
examples.zh: 示意图在成本曲线上升段标出了「价格等于边际成本」的点。

collocations: find the quantity where price equals marginal cost
compare output where price equals marginal cost

words.enDefinition: the decision whether to stop taking part in a market when all production commitments can be changed

examples.en: The long-run exit decision depended on whether the expected price would cover all costs after the lease ended.
examples.zh: 「长期退出决策」取决于租约到期后预期的售价能否覆盖所有成本。

examples.en: We compared a long-run exit decision with temporarily closing a stall while its rent remained due.
examples.zh: 我们将「长期退出决策」与仍须付租金时暂时关停摊位的情形作了比较。

collocations: compare a long-run exit decision with a short-run shutdown

words.enDefinition: an equilibrium where competitive firms have adjusted their inputs and entry or exit no longer creates further change

examples.en: In long-run competitive equilibrium, the model's identical firms earned just enough to cover all their economic costs.
examples.zh: 在「长期竞争均衡」下，模型中的同质厂商收入恰好覆盖全部经济成本。

examples.en: We marked long-run competitive equilibrium after showing how additional firms changed the price and total quantity supplied.
examples.zh: 演示新增厂商如何改变价格和总供给量后，我们标出了「长期竞争均衡」。

collocations: compare adjustment paths to long-run competitive equilibrium

words.enDefinition: a graph of quantities supplied at different prices when some inputs and the set of producers are held fixed

examples.en: The short-run supply curve showed output adjustments while the number of firms and their plant sizes stayed fixed.
examples.zh: 「短期供给曲线」显示厂商数量和工厂规模固定时的产量调整。

examples.en: We drew a short-run supply curve before allowing entry of new producers in the next part of class.
examples.zh: 我们先画「短期供给曲线」，到下一部分课程再允许新生产者进入。

collocations: read a price from a short-run supply curve

words.enDefinition: the relation between market price and total output once firms can adjust capacity and enter or exit

examples.en: The long-run industry supply changed when the model allowed additional shops to rent space in the same district.
examples.zh: 模型允许更多商店在同一区域租用场地时，「行业长期供给」改变了。

examples.en: We compared long-run industry supply under constant input costs and under rising demand for scarce locations.
examples.zh: 我们比较要素成本不变和稀缺地点需求上升两种情形下的「行业长期供给」。

collocations: explain the shape of long-run industry supply

words.enDefinition: the horizontal demand curve seen by an individual price-taking firm at the market price in the competitive model

examples.en: Our graph showed perfectly elastic firm demand at the market price while market demand sloped downward.
examples.zh: 图上总市场需求曲线向下倾斜，但「厂商的完全弹性需求」曲线在市场价格处是水平的。

examples.en: In the model, perfectly elastic firm demand meant the producer would sell nothing at a higher price.
examples.zh: 在模型里，存在「厂商的完全弹性需求」，因此生产者若定价高于市价，就什么也卖不出去。

collocations: draw a line for perfectly elastic firm demand
contrast perfectly elastic firm demand with market demand

words.enDefinition: the lowest average total cost attainable over the feasible output levels for the stated cost curve

examples.en: The curve's minimum average total cost gave the lowest break-even price available to the perfectly competitive firm.
examples.zh: 曲线的「最低平均总成本」给出了完全竞争厂商可达到的最低盈亏平衡价格。

examples.en: We compared minimum average total cost across three plants before discussing which size was cheapest at its optimum.
examples.zh: 讨论哪种规模在各自最优产量下最省成本之前，我们比较了三个工厂的「最低平均总成本」。

collocations: locate minimum average total cost on the curve
compare price with minimum average total cost

words.enDefinition: in a standard competitive short-run model, the price below which producing cannot cover avoidable variable costs

examples.en: The sample firm's shutdown price corresponded to the minimum of its average variable cost curve in class.
examples.zh: 课堂中，示例厂商的「停产价格」对应其平均变动成本曲线的最低点。

examples.en: We marked the shutdown price below the break-even level because rent had to be paid either way.
examples.zh: 无论生产与否都要付租金，因此我们把「停产价格」标在盈亏平衡价格下方。

collocations: compare prices with the shutdown price

words.enDefinition: the decision to stop current production when revenue cannot cover avoidable operating costs, given fixed commitments

examples.en: The short-run shutdown rule explained why the example's shop could keep producing despite reporting an overall loss.
examples.zh: 「短期停产规则」解释了为什么示例中的商店即使整体亏损也可能继续生产。

examples.en: We applied the short-run shutdown rule by comparing the revenue from opening with the costs it could avoid.
examples.zh: 我们比较营业所得收入和可以避免的成本，以应用「短期停产规则」。

collocations: compare the short-run shutdown rule with long-run exit

words.enDefinition: choosing the feasible decision with the smallest economic loss when all available options lead to a loss

examples.en: The model used loss minimisation to compare producing a small quantity with temporarily closing the workshop.
examples.zh: 模型通过「亏损最小化」比较少量生产与暂时关闭车间。

examples.en: We discussed loss minimisation after the exercise showed that every available output decision led to a loss.
examples.zh: 练习显示所有可选产量决策都会亏损后，我们讨论了「亏损最小化」。

collocations: choose an output for loss minimisation

words.enDefinition: the quantity producing the highest difference between total revenue and total economic cost among feasible choices

examples.en: The profit-maximising output fell when the demand curve facing the producer shifted inward in our model.
examples.zh: 在我们的模型里，生产者面对的需求曲线内移后，「利润最大化产量」下降了。

examples.en: We checked the profit-maximising output against an option of producing nothing before accepting the graph's result.
examples.zh: 在接受图上结论之前，我们把「利润最大化产量」与零产量方案作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the additional revenue per extra unit sold, or the derivative of total revenue for continuous output

examples.en: Marginal revenue was below price because the seller lowered the price on all units to sell more.
examples.zh: 卖家为增加销量调低了所有单位的价格，因此「边际收益」低于售价。

examples.en: We calculated marginal revenue from the difference between the table's receipts for two consecutive quantities sold.
examples.zh: 我们用表中相邻两种销量对应的销售收入之差，计算「边际收益」。

collocations: compare marginal revenue with marginal cost
equate marginal revenue and marginal cost

words.enDefinition: a graph showing marginal revenue at each quantity of output sold

examples.en: The marginal revenue curve lay below the single-price demand curve in the linear example drawn in class.
examples.zh: 在线性课堂示例里，「边际收益曲线」位于采用统一价格的需求曲线下方。

examples.en: We used the marginal revenue curve to locate the quantity where another sale would reduce total revenue.
examples.zh: 我们根据「边际收益曲线」找出再多卖一单位就会减少总收益的销量位置。

collocations: find where the marginal revenue curve crosses zero

words.enDefinition: a graph of the seller's total receipts across different quantities sold under the model's price schedule

examples.en: The total revenue curve initially increased as the lower price attracted enough additional customers in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，降价起初吸引了足够多的额外顾客，因此「总收益曲线」在这一段上升。

examples.en: The tutor compared the slope of the total revenue curve at two selected output levels.
examples.zh: 导师比较了「总收益曲线」在两个指定产量水平上的斜率。

collocations: find the maximum of a total revenue curve
read revenue from a total revenue curve

words.enDefinition: the ability of a buyer or seller to influence market terms such as the price it pays or charges

examples.en: The producer had market power in the example because buyers considered its specialised service difficult to replace.
examples.zh: 在示例中，买家认为该生产者的专业服务难以替代，因此它具有「市场势力」。

examples.en: We discussed why closer substitutes could reduce a firm's market power without increasing the number of sellers.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为何即使卖家数量不增加，更接近的替代品也可能削弱厂商的「市场势力」。

collocations: compete with a firm possessing market power

words.enDefinition: a producer that can choose the price of its product subject to the demand it faces

examples.en: The price-setting firm compared the profit at several prices before choosing the one paired with its preferred output.
examples.zh: 「价格制定厂商」比较几个价格下的利润，再选择与最适合的产量对应的价格。

examples.en: We showed how a price-setting firm could lose buyers if it raised the price of its service.
examples.zh: 我们演示了「价格制定厂商」提高服务价格后可能怎样流失顾客。

collocations: analyse the demand facing a price-setting firm
compare a price-setting firm with a price taker

words.enDefinition: setting prices in a market with one seller of the product and no close substitutes within the model

examples.en: The lesson compared monopoly pricing with the outcome from several identical suppliers selling the same service.
examples.zh: 这节课比较了「垄断定价」与多个相同供应者销售同一服务时的结果。

examples.en: We used monopoly pricing to explain why the model's supplier considered how its price affected total sales.
examples.zh: 我们用「垄断定价」说明模型里的供应商为何考虑价格对总销量的影响。

collocations: compare monopoly pricing with competitive pricing

words.enDefinition: the quantity chosen by the monopoly seller given its demand, costs and objective

examples.en: The monopoly output was lower than the competitive quantity under the two curves used in class.
examples.zh: 在课堂给定的需求和边际成本曲线下，「垄断产量」低于竞争产量。

examples.en: We calculated monopoly output before using the demand curve to find the price consumers would pay.
examples.zh: 我们先计算「垄断产量」，再用需求曲线找出消费者愿意支付的价格。

collocations: compare monopoly output with competitive output
find the price associated with monopoly output

words.enDefinition: the economic profit earned by the sole seller under the demand and cost conditions being analysed

examples.en: The monopoly profit changed after higher production costs were entered into the classroom model of one service provider.
examples.zh: 在课堂的单一服务供应商模型中输入更高生产成本后，「垄断利润」改变了。

examples.en: We shaded monopoly profit between price and average total cost over the quantity actually sold in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，我们按实际销量把售价与平均总成本之间的「垄断利润」区域涂上阴影。

collocations: compare monopoly profit across cost assumptions

words.enDefinition: a market situation where one producer can supply the relevant total demand at lower cost than multiple producers

examples.en: The course used a shared water network to illustrate a natural monopoly with unusually high fixed infrastructure costs.
examples.zh: 课程用共用供水网络说明固定基础设施成本特别高的「自然垄断」。

examples.en: We checked whether natural monopoly remained a credible description after the expected market demand increased.
examples.zh: 预计市场需求增大后，我们检验「自然垄断」是否仍是合理的描述。

collocations: analyse pricing in a natural monopoly

words.enDefinition: a firm with enough market influence to set its own output or price while smaller competitors respond

examples.en: The dominant firm considered how competing suppliers would respond before choosing the price in our diagram.
examples.zh: 我们图中的「主导厂商」考虑其他供应商会怎样回应，再选定价格。

examples.en: We estimated the market demand available to a dominant firm after accounting for the output of smaller suppliers.
examples.zh: 计入较小供应商的产出之后，我们估计了留给「主导厂商」的市场需求。

collocations: analyse the pricing of a dominant firm
compare a dominant firm with smaller rivals

words.enDefinition: the demand left for a particular firm at each price after subtracting the quantity supplied by competitors

examples.en: The residual demand facing the large supplier fell when the smaller firms offered more output at each price.
examples.zh: 较小厂商在各价格下提供更多产量后，大供应商面临的「剩余需求」下降了。

examples.en: We calculated residual demand at each listed price by subtracting rival supply from the total market demand.
examples.zh: 我们在各给定价格下，用市场总需求扣除竞争者供给，求出「剩余需求」。

collocations: estimate residual demand facing a firm

words.enDefinition: the combined output offered by the competitive firms outside a dominant producer in a dominant-firm model

examples.en: The fringe supply increased as smaller producers found ways to make the same service at lower cost.
examples.zh: 较小生产者找到更低成本提供同一服务的方法后，「边缘厂商供给」增加了。

examples.en: We subtracted fringe supply to estimate how much demand remained for the dominant firm at each price.
examples.zh: 我们扣除「边缘厂商供给」，估计各价格下还剩多少需求由主导厂商满足。

collocations: deduct fringe supply from market demand

words.enDefinition: the price that yields the greatest attainable profit for the producer under the stated demand and costs

examples.en: We found the profit-maximising price by reading the demand curve at the output selected in the monopoly example.
examples.zh: 我们在垄断示例所选的产量处读取需求曲线，找到「利润最大化价格」。

examples.en: The profit-maximising price in the exercise changed when customer demand became more responsive to price.
examples.zh: 顾客需求对价格更敏感后，练习中的「利润最大化价格」发生变化。

words.enDefinition: the amount by which a price exceeds the marginal cost of producing the good

examples.en: The instructor compared markup over marginal cost for two firms with different degrees of demand responsiveness.
examples.zh: 讲师比较了两家具有不同需求响应程度的厂商的「高于边际成本的加价」。

examples.en: We calculated the markup over marginal cost by subtracting the extra production cost from the listed unit price.
examples.zh: 我们从所列单位价格扣除额外生产成本，计算「高于边际成本的加价」。

collocations: calculate the markup over marginal cost
compare markup over marginal cost across products

words.enDefinition: a measure of pricing power calculated as price minus marginal cost, divided by price

examples.en: The Lerner index was zero in our competitive example because price matched the producer's marginal cost.
examples.zh: 竞争示例中，价格等于生产者的边际成本，因此「勒纳指数」为零。

examples.en: We compared the Lerner index for two hypothetical suppliers at their respective prices and marginal costs.
examples.zh: 我们根据两家假想供应商各自的价格和边际成本，比较它们的「勒纳指数」。

words.enDefinition: for an interior single-price monopoly optimum, the price-cost margin as a share of price equals the inverse magnitude of demand elasticity

examples.en: The inverse elasticity rule linked the relative price margin to the responsiveness of demand at the monopoly optimum.
examples.zh: 「逆弹性定价规则」将垄断最优点的相对价格加价与需求响应程度联系起来。

examples.en: We applied the inverse elasticity rule to two separate groups under the assumptions used in our pricing exercise.
examples.zh: 在定价练习的假设下，我们对两个分开的群体应用了「逆弹性定价规则」。

collocations: state the assumptions of the inverse elasticity rule

words.enDefinition: the total surplus lost when a monopoly reduces mutually beneficial trades relative to an efficient quantity

examples.en: The tutor shaded monopoly deadweight loss between demand and marginal cost for units the seller did not supply.
examples.zh: 导师把卖家未供应的那些单位在需求线和边际成本线之间的「垄断无谓损失」涂上阴影。

examples.en: We compared monopoly deadweight loss with the producer's profit to see why the two measures differed.
examples.zh: 我们将「垄断无谓损失」与生产者利润比较，了解两项指标为什么不同。

collocations: shade monopoly deadweight loss on a graph
compare monopoly deadweight loss across cases

words.enDefinition: charging each buyer the maximum that buyer is willing to pay for each unit under the idealised model

examples.en: The hypothetical model illustrated first-degree price discrimination by assigning each purchase its exact maximum willingness to pay.
examples.zh: 假想模型为每次购买设定其最高支付意愿对应的价格，以演示「一级价格歧视」。

examples.en: We discussed why first-degree price discrimination required information that the seller rarely possessed in actual markets.
examples.zh: 我们讨论「一级价格歧视」为什么需要卖家在真实市场里很少掌握的信息。

collocations: compare first-degree price discrimination with uniform pricing

words.enDefinition: offering pricing options that vary with quantity or product version so buyers select an option themselves

examples.en: The exercise illustrated second-degree price discrimination using different per-unit prices for small and large bundles.
examples.zh: 练习给大、小组合设定不同的单位价格，以说明「二级价格歧视」。

examples.en: We modelled second-degree price discrimination with a menu that customers could choose from without revealing their preferences directly.
examples.zh: 我们用一组方案模拟「二级价格歧视」，顾客无需直接透露自己的偏好就能选方案。

collocations: compare second-degree price discrimination with group pricing

words.enDefinition: charging different prices to distinct groups of buyers for the same product under a model of separate demands

examples.en: The museum's classroom pricing example used third-degree price discrimination by assigning separate prices to students and other visitors.
examples.zh: 课堂中的博物馆定价示例为学生和其他访客分别定价，属于「三级价格歧视」。

examples.en: We calculated the prices for third-degree price discrimination separately using each group's demand and the stated marginal cost.
examples.zh: 我们按各群体的需求与给定边际成本，分别计算「三级价格歧视」下的价格。

collocations: compare group prices under third-degree price discrimination

words.enDefinition: a price schedule comprising an access fee and a separate charge for each unit used

examples.en: The example's two-part tariff combined a membership fee with a charge for every practice room booking.
examples.zh: 示例的「两部制收费」把一笔会员费与每次练习室预订的使用费组合起来。

examples.en: We compared a two-part tariff with a single per-use charge for the same hypothetical workshop.
examples.zh: 我们把同一个假想工作坊的「两部制收费」和只按次收费作了比较。

collocations: calculate total payment under a two-part tariff

words.enDefinition: buying in a lower-price market and reselling in a higher-price market to profit from the price gap

examples.en: The classroom model tested whether resale arbitrage would narrow the price difference between the two buyer groups.
examples.zh: 课堂模型检验「转售套利」是否会缩小两个买方群体之间的价差。

examples.en: We discussed why resale arbitrage was easier for a physical textbook than for an individual swimming lesson.
examples.zh: 我们讨论为什么实体教材比一对一游泳课更容易发生「转售套利」。

collocations: account for resale arbitrage in a model

words.enDefinition: a market structure with one buyer for the input or product under consideration

examples.en: The lesson used a town with only one crop buyer to explain how monopsony affected the farmers.
examples.zh: 课堂用只有一家农作物收购商的小镇解释「买方垄断」如何影响农民。

examples.en: Our model compared monopsony with a case where several employers competed for the same pool of workers.
examples.zh: 模型比较了「买方垄断」与多个雇主争聘同一批劳动者的情形。

collocations: model a labour market under monopsony

words.enDefinition: the single buyer in a market under the monopsony model

examples.en: The monopsonist faced an upward supply curve because higher purchase prices drew more sellers into the market.
examples.zh: 「买方垄断者」面临向上倾斜的供给曲线，因为更高买价会吸引更多卖家进入市场。

examples.en: We compared the quantity a monopsonist bought with the amount purchased in the two-buyer version of the model.
examples.zh: 我们把「买方垄断者」的购买量与双买方模型中的购买量作了比较。

collocations: estimate the purchases of a monopsonist
compare a monopsonist with competing buyers

words.enDefinition: the ability of a purchaser to influence the terms paid or offered to suppliers

examples.en: The tutor described buyer market power in a market where small growers faced few alternative purchasers.
examples.zh: 导师用小种植户可选买家很少的市场说明「买方市场势力」。

examples.en: We discussed how access to a second market might reduce buyer market power in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了在课堂案例中，接入第二个市场如何可能削弱「买方市场势力」。

collocations: assess the effect of buyer market power

words.zhGloss: 具有买方势力的劳动力市场
words.enDefinition: a labour market in which employers face upward-sloping labour supply and can influence wages through hiring decisions
acceptedZhAnswers: 具有买方势力的劳动力市场

examples.en: Our monopsonistic labour market example showed how a long commute reduced the options available to job seekers.
examples.zh: 「具有买方势力的劳动力市场」示例显示，通勤时间长会减少求职者的可选岗位。

examples.en: The model compared wages in a monopsonistic labour market with those in a competitive labour market.
examples.zh: 模型比较了「具有买方势力的劳动力市场」与竞争性劳动力市场中的工资。

collocations: compare wages in a monopsonistic labour market

words.enDefinition: a graph showing the extra total expenditure from buying an additional unit of an input at each quantity

examples.en: In the single-wage model, the marginal expenditure curve lay above supply because extra hires also raised existing wages.
examples.zh: 在统一工资模型中，增聘也会提高现有员工的工资，所以「边际支出曲线」位于供给曲线上方。

examples.en: We read the marginal expenditure curve before choosing the employment level for the example's single employer.
examples.zh: 为示例中的单一雇主选定用工水平前，我们读取了「边际支出曲线」。

collocations: compare a marginal expenditure curve with the supply curve

words.enDefinition: the additional revenue generated by using one more unit of an input, holding other inputs fixed

examples.en: The marginal revenue product of an additional worker fell as the producer approached the limits of its equipment.
examples.zh: 生产者接近设备产能上限时，再雇一名工人的「边际收益产品」下降了。

examples.en: We estimated marginal revenue product from the change in receipts when one more hour of labour was added.
examples.zh: 我们用增加一小时人工后销售收入的变化估算「边际收益产品」。

collocations: compare marginal revenue product with marginal expenditure
plot the marginal revenue product curve

words.enDefinition: the marginal product of an input multiplied by the price of the output it produces

examples.en: The value of marginal product increased when output prices rose and the extra physical output remained the same.
examples.zh: 产成品价格上升而额外实物产量不变时，「边际产量价值」增加了。

examples.en: We multiplied the additional units produced by their market price to find the value of marginal product.
examples.zh: 我们将新增产量乘以市场价格，得出「边际产量价值」。

collocations: calculate the value of marginal product
compare the value of marginal product with wages
derive the value of marginal product

words.enDefinition: a graph of how much labour employers choose at each wage under the stated market and production conditions

examples.en: The labour demand curve shifted right when the competitive firms received a higher price for their output.
examples.zh: 完全竞争厂商能以更高价格卖出产品后，「劳动需求曲线」右移。

examples.en: We traced the labour demand curve while holding the price of the firm's equipment unchanged in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，我们保持厂商设备价格不变，描出「劳动需求曲线」。

words.enDefinition: demand for labour arising from customers' demand for the goods or services that workers help produce

examples.en: The exercise illustrated derived demand for labour when growing demand for repairs led the shop to hire technicians.
examples.zh: 维修需求增长，店铺因而增聘技师，练习用这一变化说明「劳动的派生需求」。

examples.en: We used derived demand for labour to explain why fewer ticket sales could reduce the need for staff.
examples.zh: 我们用「劳动的派生需求」解释为什么门票销量减少可能降低用工需求。

collocations: estimate a shift in derived demand for labour

words.enDefinition: a market with one seller and one buyer with no other trading counterparties in the relevant model

examples.en: The bilateral monopoly example paired the only component producer with the only manufacturer willing to buy its output.
examples.zh: 「双边垄断」示例把一种零件的唯一生产者与唯一愿意采购它的制造商配对。

examples.en: Our tutor used bilateral monopoly to discuss why bargaining mattered once both sides lacked alternative trading partners.
examples.zh: 导师用「双边垄断」说明，为什么两边都没有其他交易对象时，讨价还价很重要。

collocations: analyse bargaining in a bilateral monopoly
compare a bilateral monopoly with a competitive market

words.enDefinition: a market structure with many firms, differentiated products and relatively free entry and exit

examples.en: We studied monopolistic competition using several cafés that differed in location, menu and other features valued by customers.
examples.zh: 我们用几家在位置、菜单及顾客看重的其他特点上各不相同的咖啡馆学习「垄断竞争」。

examples.en: Under monopolistic competition, new sellers reduced sales for existing varieties in our simplified long-run exercise.
examples.zh: 在简化的长期练习中，「垄断竞争」下新增卖家减少了现有产品品种的销量。

collocations: analyse an industry under monopolistic competition
compare monopolistic competition with perfect competition

words.enDefinition: a product buyers perceive as different from rival products in attributes such as design, location or quality

examples.en: The differentiated product appealed to customers who wanted a quiet workspace near the railway station in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「差异化产品」吸引了想在火车站附近找安静办公场地的顾客。

examples.en: We discussed how a differentiated product could face close substitutes even when no competitor matched every feature.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了即使没有竞争者能匹配所有特点，「差异化产品」为何仍可能面对接近的替代品。

collocations: analyse demand for a differentiated product

words.enDefinition: differences in attributes for which buyers may prefer different products at the same price

examples.en: The horizontal product differentiation example offered two equal-priced flavours, and neither appealed to every customer.
examples.zh: 「横向产品差异化」示例提供两种同价口味，没有一种能吸引所有顾客。

examples.en: Our tutor explained horizontal product differentiation using preference for store location rather than a single quality ranking.
examples.zh: 导师用不同顾客对店址的偏好说明「横向产品差异化」，没有用统一的质量排名。

collocations: compare horizontal product differentiation with quality differences

words.enDefinition: differences in attributes that buyers rank by quality alike at the same price in the model

examples.en: The example used vertical product differentiation because buyers preferred the longer-lasting material when both versions cost the same.
examples.zh: 示例中买家在两版同价时都更偏好耐用材料，所以采用「纵向产品差异化」。

examples.en: We discussed vertical product differentiation after assigning a clear quality ranking to three versions of the product.
examples.zh: 为产品的三个版本明确划分质量高低后，我们讨论了「纵向产品差异化」。

collocations: rank products in a vertical product differentiation model

words.enDefinition: the range of distinct product versions available to buyers in a market

examples.en: The model predicted more product variety when new cafes could enter and serve customers with different tastes.
examples.zh: 模型预测新咖啡馆能进入市场服务口味不同的顾客时，「产品品种多样性」将提高。

examples.en: We compared the benefits of product variety with the cost of operating more production lines overall.
examples.zh: 我们将「产品品种多样性」的收益与总体运行更多生产线的成本作了比较。

words.enDefinition: competing for buyers through product features, quality, service or other attributes apart from the prices charged

examples.en: The shops used non-price competition by making their opening hours more convenient and keeping their prices unchanged.
examples.zh: 商店调整营业时间以便顾客光顾，价格维持原样，采用了「非价格竞争」。

examples.en: We considered whether improved service illustrated non-price competition when rival sellers charged the same amount per visit.
examples.zh: 当竞争者每次收费相同时，我们考虑改善服务是否体现了「非价格竞争」。

collocations: study the effects of non-price competition

words.enDefinition: the prediction in a standard monopolistic competition model that firms produce below their minimum-average-cost output in long-run equilibrium

examples.en: The tutor drew the excess capacity theorem diagram with output left of the lowest average cost point.
examples.zh: 导师画出「过剩产能定理」的示意图，产量位于平均成本最低点的左侧。

examples.en: We discussed whether the excess capacity theorem applied before assuming a downward-sloping demand curve for each firm.
examples.zh: 给各厂商设定向下倾斜的需求曲线前，我们讨论「过剩产能定理」是否适用。

collocations: state the assumptions of the excess capacity theorem
test the implications of the excess capacity theorem

words.zhGloss: 抢占既有厂商顾客的效应
words.enDefinition: the diversion of demand from existing firms to an entering firm, which reduces the incumbents' sales
acceptedZhAnswers: 抢占既有厂商顾客的效应

examples.en: The tutor explained the business-stealing effect when some regular customers switched to the new café in the model.
examples.zh: 模型里有些老顾客转去了新咖啡馆，导师借此解释「抢占既有厂商顾客的效应」。

examples.en: We compared the business-stealing effect with the additional demand created by offering a new variety of the product.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「抢占既有厂商顾客的效应」和推出新品种所创造的额外需求。

collocations: include the business-stealing effect in a model
compare the business-stealing effect across markets

words.enDefinition: a market structure in which relatively few firms account for most of the activity and closely affect one another

examples.en: The lecture described an oligopoly where each of three sellers paid close attention to the others' output decisions.
examples.zh: 课上描述了一个「寡头垄断」市场，其中三家卖家都密切关注对手的产量决策。

examples.en: We compared the oligopoly example with an industry where each of many small firms could ignore individual rivals.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「寡头垄断」示例和另一行业，在后者众多小厂商可以忽略某一家对手。

words.enDefinition: the dependence of each firm's outcome on its own choices and the choices made by rivals

examples.en: The firms showed strategic interdependence because the profit from increasing output changed when competitors expanded too.
examples.zh: 厂商增产的利润取决于对手是否也扩产，体现了「战略相互依赖」。

examples.en: We represented strategic interdependence in a table showing how different pairs of output choices affected both producers.
examples.zh: 我们用一张表列出不同的两家产量组合如何影响各方，以表示「战略相互依赖」。

words.enDefinition: rivalry in which firms compete for buyers by changing the prices they charge

examples.en: The price competition in the model intensified after a new seller offered an almost identical service.
examples.zh: 新卖家推出几乎完全相同的服务后，模型里的「价格竞争」加剧了。

examples.en: We compared price competition with a scenario where firms chose only their production quantities before any sale.
examples.zh: 我们将「价格竞争」与厂商在销售前只选择产量的情形作比较。

words.enDefinition: rivalry in which firms choose quantities and the market price depends on combined output under the model

examples.en: The quantity competition exercise asked each producer to select output before observing the resulting market price.
examples.zh: 「产量竞争」练习让各生产者先选择产量，再观察由此形成的市场价格。

examples.en: We drew each producer's preferred output for different levels of rival output in the quantity competition example.
examples.zh: 我们为「产量竞争」例题中的各生产者画出在不同对手产量下最合适的产量。

collocations: compare quantity competition with price competition

words.enDefinition: an oligopoly model where firms choose quantities simultaneously, taking rivals' quantities as given when choosing their own

examples.en: In the Cournot model, each firm chose output based on what it expected its rival to supply.
examples.zh: 在「古诺模型」中，每家厂商根据对另一家供给量的预期选择自己的产量。

examples.en: We used the Cournot model to compare industry output with the amount chosen by a single seller.
examples.zh: 我们用「古诺模型」比较行业产量与单一卖家选定的产量。

collocations: compare outputs in the Cournot model
draw response curves for a Cournot model

words.enDefinition: an oligopoly model where firms choose prices simultaneously and buyers' purchases depend on those prices

examples.en: The Bertrand model let the two producers pick prices instead of committing to production quantities in class.
examples.zh: 课堂中的「伯特兰模型」让两家生产者选择价格，无需先承诺产量。

examples.en: Our tutor changed product differentiation in the Bertrand model to show how it affected equilibrium prices.
examples.zh: 导师改变「伯特兰模型」中的产品差异程度，演示差异化程度怎样影响均衡价格。

collocations: model pricing with the Bertrand model
relax an assumption of the Bertrand model

words.enDefinition: an oligopoly model in which a leader commits to a quantity and a follower then chooses its own quantity

examples.en: The Stackelberg model allowed the first producer to commit to output before the second producer chose its output.
examples.zh: 「斯塔克尔伯格模型」允许第一家生产者先承诺产量，第二家随后决定自己的产量。

examples.en: We solved the Stackelberg model by first finding how the follower would respond to each possible leader quantity.
examples.zh: 我们先求出跟随者对领导者各可能产量的回应，再求解「斯塔克尔伯格模型」。

collocations: identify the leader in a Stackelberg model
compare quantities under the Stackelberg model

words.enDefinition: an outcome in which sellers coordinate their choices to reduce the competitive pressure among themselves

examples.en: The lesson contrasted a collusive outcome with the prices predicted when the hypothetical suppliers made decisions independently.
examples.zh: 课堂将「合谋结果」与假想供应商各自独立决策时预测得到的价格作了比较。

examples.en: Our exercise calculated total output under a collusive outcome and compared it with the competitive quantity.
examples.zh: 练习计算了「合谋结果」下的总产量，并将其与竞争产量作比较。

collocations: compare a collusive outcome with a competitive benchmark

words.enDefinition: a market whose incumbents face strong pressure from potential entrants because entry and exit can occur without significant sunk costs

examples.en: The contestable market example had only two active sellers but newcomers could rent the same equipment temporarily.
examples.zh: 「可竞争市场」示例中只有两个活跃卖家，但新进入者可以临时租用同样的设备。

examples.en: We discussed whether it remained a contestable market after adding equipment costs that entrants could not recover.
examples.zh: 模型加入进入者无法收回的设备成本后，我们讨论这个市场是否仍然是「可竞争市场」。

collocations: assess whether a market is a contestable market
compare prices in a contestable market

words.enDefinition: an expense required to enter a market that a firm cannot recover if it later leaves

examples.en: The exercise treated the custom installation as a sunk entry cost because no other producer could reuse it.
examples.zh: 由于没有其他生产者能重复利用定制装置，练习将其视为「无法收回的进入成本」。

examples.en: We compared the sunk entry cost with a lease payment that could be avoided by leaving the market.
examples.zh: 我们将「无法收回的进入成本」与退出市场后可以免去的租赁付款作了比较。

collocations: compare markets by sunk entry cost

words.enDefinition: a market where efficient firm size is sufficiently large relative to demand that only a few firms can operate efficiently

examples.en: Our tutor illustrated natural oligopoly with an industry where each efficient plant served a large share of demand.
examples.zh: 导师用单个高效工厂能满足很大一部分需求的行业演示「自然寡头结构」。

examples.en: We checked whether the industry would still have a natural oligopoly if its minimum efficient scale declined.
examples.zh: 我们核查最小有效规模降低后，该行业是否仍会形成「自然寡头结构」。

collocations: explain the emergence of a natural oligopoly
compare natural oligopoly with natural monopoly

words.enDefinition: a change in the quantity producers offer when a price, cost or other factor changes

examples.en: The supply response was small at first because the stores could not add workers immediately in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的商店不能立即增聘人手，所以最初的「供给响应」较小。

examples.en: We compared the supply response before and after firms had time to adjust their plant sizes.
examples.zh: 在厂商有时间调整工厂规模前后，我们比较了「供给响应」。

collocations: allow for a delayed supply response

words.enDefinition: the extent to which a change in a producer's costs changes the price charged to buyers

examples.en: The cost pass-through was incomplete because the example seller absorbed part of the increase in input prices.
examples.zh: 示例卖家吸收了要素涨价的一部分，所以「成本传导」不完全。

examples.en: We compared cost pass-through across two markets where sellers faced buyers with different demand responsiveness.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个市场的「成本传导」，两地买家对价格的响应程度不同。

collocations: compare cost pass-through across market structures

words.enDefinition: temporary entry to serve a profitable portion of a market, followed by exit with little unrecoverable cost in the contestable-market model

examples.en: The lecture used hit-and-run entry to explain why the model's incumbents faced pressure despite having few active competitors.
examples.zh: 课堂用「短期进入后退出」解释，为什么即使活跃竞争者很少，模型中的既有厂商也面临压力。

examples.en: We compared hit-and-run entry with entering a market that required expensive installations with no resale value.
examples.zh: 我们将「短期进入后退出」与进入一个须配备昂贵且没有转售价值的设施的市场作了比较。

collocations: explain the threat of hit-and-run entry

words.enDefinition: the way the set of firms in a market changes over time as producers join or leave

examples.en: The entry and exit dynamics in our model slowly changed the number of sellers after demand increased.
examples.zh: 需求增加后，模型的「企业进入与退出动态」逐步改变了卖家数量。

examples.en: We discussed entry and exit dynamics for the industry after switching from a short-run to a long-run model.
examples.zh: 从短期模型转为长期模型后，我们讨论该行业的「企业进入与退出动态」。

collocations: compare entry and exit dynamics across markets
